metadata.title: Product Streams
metadata.description: Outcome-based product streams for the Transport Management and Freight Exchange domain: the shipper lifecycle (procure, plan, execute, track, settle, analyze), the carrier-side exchange and trust journeys, and site dock operations across a network of 80,000+ carriers in 80 countries.
metadata.flowModelNote: Each stream carries only stream-specific flows and names the supporting bricks used in each step.

rootGroups.name: Shipper Journeys
rootGroups.description: The end-to-end lifecycle an enterprise shipper runs on the platform: procure capacity, plan loads, execute orders, track shipments, settle invoices, and analyze the network.

streams.name: Procure Freight Capacity
streams.description: Take a transportation director from a transport RFP through bid rounds and negotiation to signed rate cards and routing guides that planning and execution consume directly.
outcomes: Lower transport cost per shipment versus market benchmarks
Contracted capacity coverage secured before the season starts, wired straight into daily execution

flows.title: Procure Freight Capacity
flows.description: From lane baseline to awarded contracts and activated routing guides.

steps.title: Build the lane and volume baseline
keyFacts: A pan-European shipper tenders hundreds of lanes across plants, DCs, and borders in one yearly event.
Executed cost and volume history from the same platform gives a baseline offline procurement never has.
painPoints: Baselines assembled from ERP extracts and spreadsheets are stale before the RFP launches.
Ambiguous lane and equipment definitions are the top cause of unusable carrier bids.

dependencies.name: Logistics Master Data
dependencies.description: Shared locations, lanes, and equipment definitions.
dependencies.how: Keeps tendered lanes on the same definitions planning and execution use.

steps.title: Launch RFP rounds to the carrier market
keyFacts: Digital tendering reaches incumbents and new capacity from a network of 80,000+ carriers across 80 countries.
Structured bid sheets keep thousands of line-item bids comparable across multi-round RFPs.
painPoints: Email tenders drown transport directors in inconsistent spreadsheets that take weeks to normalize.
Inviting only incumbents hides the real market price and leaves gaps on new lanes.

dependencies.name: Freight Procurement and Tendering
dependencies.description: Runs RFPs, bid rounds, and structured bid collection.
dependencies.how: Publishes the event, invites carriers, and collects structured bids per lane.

steps.title: Compare bids against market benchmarks
keyFacts: Comparison weighs price, capacity commitment, service history, and compliance — not price alone.
Lane benchmarks from network transaction data show whether a bid sits above or below market.
painPoints: Without benchmarks, an aggressive bid and an unsustainable one look identical until execution fails.
Awarding purely on price selects carriers who decline tenders when the spot market pays better.

dependencies.name: Transport Analytics and Benchmarking
dependencies.description: Lane rate benchmarks from network transactions.
dependencies.how: Positions every bid against the market rate for its lane.

steps.title: Negotiate and award capacity
keyFacts: Final rounds run inside the tool, so the audit trail of offers and counteroffers is complete.
Key lanes are deliberately awarded to a primary plus backups to balance cost and capacity risk.
painPoints: Negotiations that drift to phone and email lose the audit trail and breed disputes over what was agreed.
Single-carrier awards on critical lanes turn every hiccup into a spot-market emergency.

dependencies.name: Freight Procurement and Tendering
dependencies.description: Manages negotiation rounds and documented awards.
dependencies.how: Runs final rounds and records the award per lane and carrier.

steps.title: Activate rate cards and routing guides
keyFacts: Awarded rates become structured rate cards with validity, surcharges, and fuel-indexation rules.
Because procurement and execution share one platform, activated rates govern carrier selection the next morning.
painPoints: Rate cards trapped in PDFs never reach daily carrier selection, so negotiated savings evaporate.
Unmanaged surcharge and fuel-index rules cause invoice disputes months later.

dependencies.name: Rates and Contract Management
dependencies.description: Stores contracted rates, surcharges, and indexation rules.
dependencies.how: Turns awards into executable rate cards with full surcharge logic.

dependencies.name: Carrier Selection and Load Tendering
dependencies.description: Applies routing guides and cascades to daily loads.
dependencies.how: Lets the awarded routing guide drive daily tender sequences.

streams.name: Plan and Optimize Transport
streams.description: Turn raw ERP orders into an optimized, tendable load plan: consolidate orders into full loads, choose routes and equipment, and assign carriers per routing guide.
outcomes: Fewer planner touches per load through automated consolidation and carrier assignment
Higher vehicle fill and a load plan that is executable as tendered

flows.title: Plan and Optimize Transport
flows.description: From incoming ERP orders to a released, carrier-assigned load plan.

steps.title: Ingest orders from ERP systems
keyFacts: Deliveries and transport requirements flow continuously from SAP and other ERPs into managed transport orders.
Order data quality — weights, time windows, incoterms — determines how much of planning can be automated.
painPoints: Orders arriving by email or CSV force re-keying, introducing errors that surface at the dock.
Missing weights and time windows push automatable loads into manual planning.

dependencies.name: ERP and Systems Integration Hub
dependencies.description: Connects shipper ERP and order systems to the platform.
dependencies.how: Receives orders and status updates without manual entry.

steps.title: Consolidate orders into loads
keyFacts: Consolidation groups compatible orders by lane, date, and equipment into full truckloads and multi-stop tours.
Around one in five truck kilometers in Europe runs empty, so every avoided partial load matters for cost and CO2.
painPoints: Manual consolidation leaves obvious combinations on the table, shipping air at full-truck prices.
Constraints living in planners' heads make the plan collapse when the planner is on holiday.

dependencies.name: Transport Planning and Optimization
dependencies.description: Builds and optimizes loads and tours from open orders.
dependencies.how: Proposes consolidated loads and tours from the open order pool.

steps.title: Optimize routes, equipment, and schedule
keyFacts: Optimization weighs cost, transit time, delivery windows, and emissions across the proposed loads.
EU driving-time regulations cap what a driver can legally cover per day, so feasibility checks are built in.
painPoints: Optimizers that ignore driving-time rules produce plans carriers cannot legally execute.
Plans optimized purely on cost create window violations that cost more in penalties than they saved.

dependencies.name: Transport Planning and Optimization
dependencies.description: Optimizes route, equipment, and schedule per load.
dependencies.how: Finalizes routes and schedules that are efficient and feasible.

steps.title: Assign carriers per routing guide
keyFacts: Each load gets its carrier cascade from the routing guide, with contracted rates attached at assignment.
Loads without contracted coverage are flagged early for the spot process, not discovered on dispatch day.
painPoints: Assignment by planner habit routes freight to favorite carriers instead of contracted ones.
Late discovery of uncovered lanes forces panic spot buying at peak rates.

dependencies.name: Carrier Selection and Load Tendering
dependencies.description: Applies routing guides and prepares tender cascades.
dependencies.how: Attaches the contracted cascade and rates to every planned load.

steps.title: Release the load plan for execution
keyFacts: Released loads carry all data needed for tendering, documents, and tracking into the execution pipeline.
A clean handover lets execution run at thousands of loads per day without planners re-touching each one.
painPoints: Plans exported to another system for execution drift out of sync the moment anything changes.
Untracked late changes send carriers to loads that were cancelled or moved.

dependencies.name: Transport Order Management
dependencies.description: Tracks order and load state through release and amendment.
dependencies.how: Hands released loads to execution with consistent state and amendment history.

streams.name: Execute Transport Orders
streams.description: Move every planned load through tender, acceptance, dispatch, and documented delivery via the connected carrier network — API-first execution that scales to thousands of loads per day.
outcomes: High first-tender acceptance through contracted cascades and connected carriers
Digital delivery evidence (eCMR, POD) ready for settlement the moment the truck leaves

flows.title: Execute Transport Orders
flows.description: From released load to accepted, dispatched, and documented delivery.

steps.title: Tender the load to contracted carriers
keyFacts: Tenders follow the routing-guide cascade automatically — primary first, backups on timeout or rejection.
The API-first model, relaunched as Transport Execution in January 2026, wires shipper ERP/TMS straight into the carrier network.
painPoints: Phone-and-email tendering caps planner throughput and leaves no record of who declined what.
Cascades without deadlines stall loads while everyone waits for a carrier who will never answer.

dependencies.name: Transport Execution Orchestration
dependencies.description: Orchestrates order execution across shipper systems and the network.
dependencies.how: Drives the tender lifecycle at API speed and volume.

dependencies.name: Carrier Selection and Load Tendering
dependencies.description: Runs the tender cascade with rates and deadlines.
dependencies.how: Executes the cascade per the routing guide with enforced response windows.

steps.title: Carrier accepts or rejects digitally
keyFacts: Carriers respond via portal, mobile app, or their own dispatch system through API/EDI — whichever fits their size.
Digital acceptance creates a binding, timestamped commitment with the agreed rate attached.
painPoints: Small carriers fall out of digital processes unless the portal and app are genuinely easy.
Verbal acceptances create disputes when rate or load details were misheard.

dependencies.name: Carrier Portal and Mobile
dependencies.description: Web and mobile access to tenders, loads, and documents.
dependencies.how: Lets carriers of any size accept and manage loads digitally.

dependencies.name: Carrier Connectivity Gateway
dependencies.description: Connects carrier TMS and dispatch systems via API and EDI.
dependencies.how: Lets integrated carriers respond system-to-system without portal logins.

steps.title: Escalate uncovered loads
keyFacts: Loads that exhaust their cascade are flagged with time-to-pickup context and a direct path to the spot market.
Uncovered-load patterns per lane feed the next procurement cycle as evidence of capacity gaps.
painPoints: Silent tender failures are discovered only when the dock asks where the truck is.
Repeated escalations on the same lane signal a broken routing guide nobody is fixing.

dependencies.name: Notifications and Messaging
dependencies.description: Delivers alerts across web, mobile, and email.
dependencies.how: Alerts planners the moment a cascade is exhausted.

steps.title: Dispatch and confirm pickup details
keyFacts: Accepted loads carry confirmed pickup windows, dock references, and driver and vehicle details before the truck rolls.
Driver and plate details shared in advance speed up gate check-in at security-conscious sites.
painPoints: Trucks arriving without announced driver details get held at the gate, burning slot time.
Pickup details changed by phone never reach the driver actually doing the job.

dependencies.name: Transport Execution Orchestration
dependencies.description: Coordinates dispatch data between shipper, carrier, and site.
dependencies.how: Confirms pickup windows, vehicle, and driver assignments digitally.

steps.title: Document the transport and confirm delivery
keyFacts: Consignment notes and loading documents are generated from order data; eCMR adoption is spreading as European countries ratify the protocol.
Drivers capture signature, photos, and remarks in the app — the digital POD starts the settlement clock the same day.
painPoints: Paper CMRs get lost or sit in truck cabins for weeks, delaying payment and poisoning carrier relations.
Undocumented delivery deviations turn into unresolvable claims months later.

dependencies.name: e-Documents (eCMR, POD)
dependencies.description: Digital consignment notes and proof-of-delivery capture.
dependencies.how: Issues eCMR from order data and attaches the signed POD in real time.

dependencies.name: Transport Order Management
dependencies.description: Closes the order lifecycle with delivery confirmation.
dependencies.how: Marks the order delivered and releases it to settlement.

streams.name: Track and Manage Exceptions
streams.description: Keep every dispatched order visible from pickup to delivery with live ETAs, detect disruptions early, and resolve them before the shipper's customer notices.
outcomes: High track-and-trace coverage across contracted and spot carriers
Exceptions resolved before they become customer-facing failures

flows.title: Track and Manage Exceptions
flows.description: From dispatched order to delivered, with live ETA and managed disruptions.

steps.title: Capture position and status events
keyFacts: Position data flows in from carrier telematics, driver mobile apps, and carrier TMS integrations.
In Europe's fragmented carrier market, the mobile app is often the only viable tracking source for small carriers.
painPoints: Tracking coverage collapses on the last leg when subcontracted carriers are not connected.
Every uncovered load means a planner phoning a dispatcher who phones a driver.

dependencies.name: Carrier Connectivity Gateway
dependencies.description: Integrates telematics, EDI, and API event sources.
dependencies.how: Normalizes events from heterogeneous carrier systems into one stream.

steps.title: Compute live ETAs per stop
keyFacts: ETAs combine live position, route, traffic, remaining driving-time budget, and planned stops.
A late truck often cannot simply drive faster — mandatory EU rest periods add hours a naive map estimate misses.
painPoints: Map-only ETAs that ignore rest obligations are systematically optimistic and destroy trust in the tool.
Stakeholders computing their own estimates guarantee contradictory answers to the same customer.

dependencies.name: Real-Time Visibility and ETA
dependencies.description: Computes and publishes live ETAs from the event stream.
dependencies.how: Maintains one authoritative ETA per stop for all consumers.

steps.title: Detect deviations and raise exceptions
keyFacts: Rules watch for late departures, ETA drift beyond windows, missed milestones, and silent loads with no signal.
The exception queue, not the shipment list, is the planner's workspace — healthy loads manage themselves.
painPoints: Alert floods train planners to ignore the dashboard, which is worse than no alerts.
Silent failures — loads with no events at all — are the easiest to miss and the most expensive.

dependencies.name: Exception Management
dependencies.description: Detects, classifies, and queues shipment exceptions.
dependencies.how: Turns deviation signals into a prioritized work queue.

steps.title: Notify stakeholders and collaborate on resolution
keyFacts: Exception context — order, carrier, position, ETA impact — is shared with carrier and receiving site in one thread.
Proactive delay notice to the customer converts a service failure into a managed expectation.
painPoints: Resolution scattered over phone and email leaves no record and repeats the same investigation twice.
Customers who learn about a delay from the empty dock churn faster than those who got a warning.

dependencies.name: Notifications and Messaging
dependencies.description: Targeted alerts and shared communication threads.
dependencies.how: Informs the right stakeholders with live exception context.

dependencies.name: Carrier Portal and Mobile
dependencies.description: Brings the executing carrier into the thread.
dependencies.how: Lets the carrier respond in the same shared context.

steps.title: Resolve, re-plan, and close the shipment
keyFacts: Resolution ranges from rebooking the dock slot to re-tendering the remainder of a failed transport, with all systems updated consistently.
Closure stamps actual arrival against the promised window — the on-time actuals carrier reviews and analytics run on.
painPoints: Recovery decided in one system but not propagated leaves docks, customers, and invoices on the old plan.
Shipments that never formally close pollute on-time statistics and dangle in settlement.

dependencies.name: Exception Management
dependencies.description: Drives resolution workflows and records outcomes.
dependencies.how: Executes and documents the chosen recovery path with reason codes.

dependencies.name: Transport Order Management
dependencies.description: Keeps order state consistent through re-planning and closure.
dependencies.how: Propagates recovery decisions and closes the delivered order.

streams.name: Settle and Audit Freight
streams.description: Turn proof of delivery into audited, correctly priced invoices — self-billing where possible, automated audit everywhere else — and secure the payment flow for carriers.
outcomes: Every freight invoice audited against contracted rates automatically instead of sampled manually
Shorter carrier payment cycles through self-billing, digital POD, and payment guarantees

flows.title: Settle and Audit Freight
flows.description: From proof of delivery to audited invoice, self-billing, and secured payment.

steps.title: Accrue expected costs per order
keyFacts: Expected cost is computed at tender acceptance from the rate card, surcharges, and fuel indexation — before any invoice exists.
Every later invoice line is compared against this expected cost, which is what makes automated audit possible.
painPoints: Without accruals, freight spend is only known when invoices arrive weeks later, wrecking budget control.
Rate cards not maintained in a system make expected cost a matter of opinion.

dependencies.name: Freight Cost Management
dependencies.description: Computes and accrues expected transport costs per order.
dependencies.how: Accrues the expected cost from contracted rates at acceptance.

dependencies.name: Rates and Contract Management
dependencies.description: Contracted rates, surcharges, and indexation rules.
dependencies.how: Serves as the pricing source of truth for every accrual.

steps.title: Audit invoices or generate self-billing
keyFacts: In self-billing, the shipper generates the invoice from confirmed execution data and digital POD — removing mismatch entirely.
Automated audit checks every line against expected cost and delivery evidence, flagging only genuine discrepancies.
painPoints: Manual invoice checking scales linearly with volume, so most invoices are effectively unchecked.
Small recurring overcharges compound into material annual leakage across thousands of loads.

dependencies.name: Freight Audit and Self-Billing
dependencies.description: Automated invoice audit and self-billing generation.
dependencies.how: Audits every line or replaces carrier invoicing with self-billing.

dependencies.name: e-Documents (eCMR, POD)
dependencies.description: Digital delivery evidence linked to orders.
dependencies.how: Supplies POD and eCMR evidence settlement verifies automatically.

steps.title: Resolve discrepancies and disputes
keyFacts: Flagged lines route into a structured workflow with order, rate, and evidence attached — both sides see the same data.
Dispute patterns per carrier and surcharge type feed back into rate-card cleanup and the next tender.
painPoints: Email dispute threads without shared evidence run for months and sour carrier relationships.
Recurring disputes on the same surcharge signal a broken rate card nobody owns.

dependencies.name: Freight Audit and Self-Billing
dependencies.description: Dispute workflows on flagged invoice lines.
dependencies.how: Runs evidence-backed dispute resolution.

steps.title: Post approved costs to ERP finance
keyFacts: Approved invoices and self-bills post to the shipper's ERP with cost allocation to plant, product line, or customer order.
Auditable order-to-payment lineage is what lets internal audit and CSRD reporting trust the freight numbers.
painPoints: Manual re-entry of freight invoices into ERP re-introduces the errors the audit just removed.
Cost allocation done quarterly by spreadsheet makes freight cost per product a fiction.

dependencies.name: ERP and Systems Integration Hub
dependencies.description: Posts settlement results into shipper finance systems.
dependencies.how: Posts approved costs and allocations into ERP automatically.

steps.title: Secure the carrier payment flow
keyFacts: Payment guarantee services protect carriers against non-payment on network transactions.
Predictable payment is a top decision factor for carriers — days sales outstanding is a survival metric for small fleets.
painPoints: Non-payment risk keeps small carriers away from otherwise attractive cross-border freight.
A single large unpaid invoice can push an owner-operator into insolvency.

dependencies.name: Payment Guarantee and Collections
dependencies.description: Payment guarantees and collections for network transactions.
dependencies.how: Secures carrier payment and manages collection cases.

streams.name: Analyze Network Performance
streams.description: Turn the platform's transaction flow — orders, tenders, tracking events, invoices — into cost, service, and CO2 insight and lane benchmarks that change procurement, planning, and carrier decisions.
outcomes: Transport cost per shipment positioned against market benchmarks per lane
Carrier and lane decisions driven by measured performance, with audit-ready CO2 reporting

flows.title: Analyze Network Performance
flows.description: From transaction data to cost, service, and CO2 insight that feeds back into decisions.

steps.title: Consolidate cost, service, and event data
keyFacts: Analytics draws on the platform's own flow — hundreds of thousands of freight transactions and offers daily.
Orders, tenders, tracking actuals, and audited invoices join on shared master data, so cost and service describe the same shipment.
painPoints: Analytics bolted onto exported spreadsheets is outdated on arrival and trusted by no one.
Cost and service data keyed differently make cost-versus-service trade-offs unanswerable.

dependencies.name: Transport Analytics and Benchmarking
dependencies.description: Consolidates and models platform transaction data.
dependencies.how: Builds the consolidated analytical dataset across cost, service, and events.

steps.title: Benchmark lane rates against the market
keyFacts: Network transaction data supports lane-level market benchmarks a single shipper could never compute alone.
Cost versus market per lane is the transportation director's north-star view — it separates a good rate from a merely stable one.
painPoints: Without benchmarks, a shipper only learns their rates were high when a competitor ships cheaper.
Annual consultancy benchmark studies are obsolete the quarter after delivery.

dependencies.name: Transport Analytics and Benchmarking
dependencies.description: Computes lane rate benchmarks from network data.
dependencies.how: Positions contracted and spot rates against the lane market.

steps.title: Measure carrier and lane service performance
keyFacts: On-time performance, tender acceptance, tracking coverage, and claim rates are computed from execution actuals.
Scorecards built from shared platform data are accepted by carriers because both sides see the same numbers.
painPoints: Carrier reviews based on remembered incidents reward the loudest account manager, not the best carrier.
Scorecards carriers dispute on data grounds change nothing.

dependencies.name: Real-Time Visibility and ETA
dependencies.description: Supplies confirmed arrival actuals per shipment.
dependencies.how: Provides the ground-truth actuals behind service scorecards.

steps.title: Report transport emissions
keyFacts: Shipment-level CO2 is computed from actual distances, loads, and equipment, aligned to accepted logistics accounting frameworks.
CSRD brings transport emissions into audited corporate reporting for large EU companies, moving CO2 from marketing to compliance.
painPoints: Spend-based emission estimates are too crude to defend in an audit or steer real consolidation decisions.
Emission reporting disconnected from planning cannot show which action would actually cut CO2.

dependencies.name: Emissions Reporting
dependencies.description: Computes and reports shipment-level transport emissions.
dependencies.how: Produces audit-ready CO2 figures from actual shipment data.

steps.title: Feed insight back into procurement and planning
keyFacts: Benchmark gaps, capacity-shortage patterns, and service outliers translate into tender scopes and routing-guide changes.
The analytics-to-action loop is what converts a reporting product into a network advantage.
painPoints: Dashboards nobody acts on are cost, not insight.
Insight that arrives after the yearly tender closes waits a year to matter.

dependencies.name: Freight Cost Management
dependencies.description: Order-level cost records for spend analysis.
dependencies.how: Provides the audited cost base behind spend and savings analysis.

dependencies.name: ERP and Systems Integration Hub
dependencies.description: Delivers analytical outputs into shipper BI systems.
dependencies.how: Pushes insight into the systems where decisions are made.

rootGroups.name: Carrier and Network Journeys
rootGroups.description: The carrier-side journeys on the freight exchange network: matching spot freight with truck capacity, and joining a vetted, trusted, fraud-screened network.

streams.name: Match Spot Freight
streams.description: Take a posted spot load or a free truck to a matched, booked deal on the exchange — the Teleroute, Wtransnet, and Bursa Transport journey that keeps 80,000+ carriers loaded in both directions across 80 countries.
outcomes: Fewer empty kilometers through fast return-load coverage
Uncovered shipper loads closed on the spot market within hours, not days

flows.title: Match Spot Freight
flows.description: From posted load or free truck to a matched, booked, and confirmed deal.

steps.title: Post a spot load or free capacity
keyFacts: Both sides post: shippers and forwarders publish loads, carriers publish free trucks with position and availability.
Hundreds of thousands of freight transactions and offers flow through the network daily across 80 countries.
painPoints: Vague postings generate calls instead of matches and waste dispatcher time on both sides.
Posting the same load on several exchanges and forgetting to retract it creates double-booking chaos.

dependencies.name: Freight Exchange Marketplace
dependencies.description: Hosts spot freight and capacity postings across the network.
dependencies.how: Publishes structured load and capacity offers to the network.

steps.title: Search and receive matched recommendations
keyFacts: Matching ranks offers by lane fit, dates, equipment, price context, and counterparty quality — not just newest first.
Return-load recommendations near a truck's delivery point attack the roughly one-in-five empty-kilometer share of European road freight.
painPoints: In a raw list of thousands of offers, good return loads expire before a dispatcher scrolls to them.
Matches that ignore equipment or ADR constraints waste the calls they trigger.

dependencies.name: Freight Matching and Recommendations
dependencies.description: Ranks and recommends load-truck matches across the network.
dependencies.how: Surfaces the best-fitting counterpart offers first.

dependencies.name: Notifications and Messaging
dependencies.description: Match alerts on saved searches and lanes.
dependencies.how: Pushes matching offers to dispatchers in real time.

steps.title: Check the counterparty before committing
keyFacts: Every offer shows the counterparty's vetting status, trust indicators, and network history before any commitment.
Cargo crime and identity fraud are persistent, documented risks in European road freight — counterparty checks are a survival habit.
painPoints: One fraudulent counterparty can cost a small carrier a full load's value or an entire cargo.
Manual background checking per deal is impossible at spot-market speed.

dependencies.name: Trust Scores and Fraud Prevention
dependencies.description: Counterparty trust signals and fraud screening.
dependencies.how: Shows vetting status and risk signals on every offer.

steps.title: Negotiate and book the deal
keyFacts: Price and conditions are agreed in the platform, producing a documented transaction both sides can rely on.
A booked exchange deal carries the references settlement and payment-guarantee services later need.
painPoints: Deals closed by phone leave price and conditions undocumented when a dispute appears.
Slow negotiation loses the truck — spot capacity is gone in minutes at busy times.

dependencies.name: Freight Exchange Marketplace
dependencies.description: Handles offer negotiation and deal booking.
dependencies.how: Closes and documents the transaction.

steps.title: Confirm execution details and hand over
keyFacts: The booked deal is confirmed with driver, vehicle, and loading references through the carrier portal or app.
Spot deals flow into the same execution and tracking rails as contracted freight — one process for the carrier.
painPoints: Spot loads executed outside the system lose tracking, documents, and payment protection at once.
Missing loading references strand drivers at gates while the slot expires.

dependencies.name: Carrier Portal and Mobile
dependencies.description: Carries confirmation details to carrier and driver.
dependencies.how: Confirms execution details and connects the deal to execution.

streams.name: Onboard and Trust the Network
streams.description: Take a carrier from signup to vetted, rated, fraud-screened network member — and keep the trust current for as long as they trade. Trust is what lets 80,000+ carriers and thousands of shippers transact with strangers safely.
outcomes: New carriers vetted and productive quickly without diluting trust standards
Fraudulent actors kept out or removed before they can steal loads or money

flows.title: Onboard and Trust the Network
flows.description: From carrier signup to vetted, continuously monitored network membership.

steps.title: Register the company and verify identity
keyFacts: Signup captures legal entity, registration numbers, and authorized users, verified against business registries.
Identity fraud — criminals impersonating legitimate carriers to steal cargo — is a known attack pattern, so identity is the first trust gate.
painPoints: Weak identity checks at signup poison every downstream trust signal the network produces.
Re-registering separately per product frustrates carriers and fragments their track record.

dependencies.name: Identity and Organization Management
dependencies.description: Organizations, users, and verified identities platform-wide.
dependencies.how: Establishes one verified organization identity for all products.

steps.title: Screen licenses, insurance, and documents
keyFacts: Vetting checks transport licenses, insurance certificates, VAT status, and sanctions exposure before membership is granted.
Documents carry expiry dates; validity is tracked continuously, not checked once at signup.
painPoints: Expired insurance discovered after a cargo claim is a catastrophe for everyone involved.
Manual document chasing at scale either blocks growth or quietly lowers the bar.

dependencies.name: Carrier Vetting and Compliance
dependencies.description: Screens and monitors licenses, insurance, and compliance documents.
dependencies.how: Enforces document validity at onboarding and continuously after.

steps.title: Activate membership, billing, and access
keyFacts: Approved carriers get exchange access, portal and mobile accounts, and a subscription matching their size and product mix.
Fast activation matters commercially — a carrier who cannot trade for weeks churns before their first load.
painPoints: Vetting rigor that turns into weeks of onboarding delay hands growth to less careful competitors.
Billing surprises in the first month are a leading cause of early membership cancellation.

dependencies.name: Subscription and Usage Billing
dependencies.description: Memberships, subscriptions, and usage metering.
dependencies.how: Activates and meters the carrier's membership from day one.

dependencies.name: Carrier Portal and Mobile
dependencies.description: The carrier's daily working environment.
dependencies.how: Gives the activated carrier immediate access to loads and tools.

steps.title: Build trust scores and monitor fraud continuously
keyFacts: Completed transactions, payment behavior, and counterparty feedback accumulate into a living trust profile that boosts matching visibility.
Continuous monitoring watches for account takeover, behavior shifts, and known fraud signatures — cargo theft via fake carriers is organized crime with real losses across Europe.
painPoints: A vetted account taken over by fraudsters is more dangerous than an obvious fake, because it inherits earned trust.
Scores that can be gamed with fake transactions are worse than no scores.

dependencies.name: Trust Scores and Fraud Prevention
dependencies.description: Trust scoring and continuous fraud detection.
dependencies.how: Maintains earned, hard-to-game trust profiles and acts on fraud signals fast.

steps.title: Back membership with payment security
keyFacts: Payment guarantees let carriers accept loads from unfamiliar counterparties knowing payment is protected.
Collections handled centrally spare small carriers cross-border legal chasing they cannot afford.
painPoints: Fear of non-payment keeps owner-operators off cross-border loads that would cut their empty kilometers.
Chasing a foreign debtor through another country's courts costs more than most single invoices are worth.

dependencies.name: Payment Guarantee and Collections
dependencies.description: Payment guarantees and centralized collections.
dependencies.how: Protects members' revenue on network transactions.

rootGroups.name: Site Operations
rootGroups.description: The dock and yard journey at plants and distribution centers, where transport plans meet physical loading capacity.

streams.name: Schedule Docks and Yards
streams.description: Turn booked transports into confirmed dock slots and fast site turnarounds: publish site capacity, let carriers self-book, absorb ETA changes, and run the gate-to-gate flow.
outcomes: Shorter truck turnaround times at plants and DCs
Dock utilization smoothed across the day, with timestamped events ending waiting-time disputes

flows.title: Schedule Docks and Yards
flows.description: From booked transport to confirmed slot, fast turnaround, and measured site performance.

steps.title: Publish site slot capacity
keyFacts: Sites define docks, operating hours, slot lengths, and handling constraints per equipment and goods type.
Published capacity turns arrival management from first-come-first-served queues into scheduled flow.
painPoints: Unscheduled sites concentrate arrivals into morning peaks that create long queues and afternoon idle docks.
Slot definitions that ignore handling constraints produce bookings the site cannot actually serve.

dependencies.name: Dock Scheduling
dependencies.description: Site dock capacity, slots, and booking rules.
dependencies.how: Publishes bookable capacity that reflects real site constraints.

dependencies.name: Logistics Master Data
dependencies.description: Site, dock, and equipment definitions.
dependencies.how: Aligns slot definitions with the platform-wide site model.

steps.title: Carrier books a slot for the transport
keyFacts: Carriers self-book slots against their confirmed transports through the portal or app — no phone tag with the site office.
Slot bookings link to the transport order, so site staff see what is arriving, from whom, with which references.
painPoints: Phone-and-email slot booking consumes site office hours and still produces double bookings.
Slots not linked to transport orders leave the site guessing what a booked truck actually carries.

dependencies.name: Carrier Portal and Mobile
dependencies.description: Self-service slot booking for carriers.
dependencies.how: Serves as the carrier's booking interface tied to their transports.

dependencies.name: Transport Order Management
dependencies.description: Links slot bookings to transport orders.
dependencies.how: Gives every slot booking full order context.

steps.title: Adjust slots when ETAs change
keyFacts: Live ETAs flag slot conflicts hours in advance — a truck running two hours late frees its slot for reassignment.
Late-arrival patterns per carrier and lane feed the site's planning assumptions and carrier reviews.
painPoints: Sites that learn about delays at the gate hold empty docks for absent trucks while present trucks wait.
Manual rebooking by phone cannot keep up on a day when weather delays half the inbound flow.

dependencies.name: Real-Time Visibility and ETA
dependencies.description: Live ETAs against booked slots.
dependencies.how: Detects slot conflicts before the truck arrives.

dependencies.name: Notifications and Messaging
dependencies.description: Alerts site and carrier to slot changes.
dependencies.how: Coordinates rebooking between site and carrier in time to matter.

steps.title: Check the truck in at the gate
keyFacts: Gate check-in matches the arriving truck against the booking — driver, plate, references — and timestamps the arrival.
Arrival timestamps start the objective clock behind every later waiting-time discussion.
painPoints: Unannounced trucks trigger manual verification that queues everyone behind them.
Without timestamps, waiting-time claims are negotiations, not facts.

dependencies.name: Dock Scheduling
dependencies.description: Gate check-in against bookings with timestamps.
dependencies.how: Verifies arrivals against bookings and records gate events.

steps.title: Load or unload and release the truck
keyFacts: Yard statuses (called forward, at dock, loading, complete) keep drivers, dock teams, and planners on one picture.
Fast release matters to carriers directly: turnaround time is lost driving time under EU driving-hours limits.
painPoints: Drivers idling in yards without call-forward information block parking and miss their legal driving windows.
Sites without handling-time data cannot tell which dock, product, or shift causes slow turnarounds.

dependencies.name: Dock Scheduling
dependencies.description: Yard and dock statuses through handling.
dependencies.how: Runs the called-forward-to-release flow with full timestamps.

dependencies.name: Carrier Portal and Mobile
dependencies.description: Live yard status and call-forward notices for drivers.
dependencies.how: Keeps the driver informed from gate to release.

steps.title: Review site turnaround performance
keyFacts: Turnaround time, slot utilization, and late-arrival shares are computed from gate and dock timestamps per site and carrier.
Site metrics separate carrier lateness from site slowness — ending the standing argument about whose fault the queue is.
painPoints: Sites managed on anecdote fix the wrong bottleneck and keep the queues.
Without shared metrics, carriers and sites blame each other for the same wasted hours indefinitely.

dependencies.name: Dock Scheduling
dependencies.description: Timestamped site event data for performance metrics.
dependencies.how: Serves as the source of truth for turnaround and utilization measurement.
